title: Upgrade bd 1.1.0 to 1.3.0 across all beads repos
description: Upgrade the shared bd binary (1.1.0, embedded mode) and migrate every Beads database on this machine to the target release. Principles: docs/beads-upgrades.md. Machine inventory (databases, main clones, worktrees, second binary, baselines): gitignored beads-upgrade.local.md. Upstream guide: https://beads.gascity.com/getting-started/upgrading
design: Revised plan 2026-09-30 (supersedes the original 7 steps). (0) Owner decides target (1.3.0 vs wait for 1.3.1 GA) and confirms no other machine/cloud clone holds unpushed Dolt commits. (1) Download pinned release asset, verify checksums.txt; rehearse on copies of every database with the Dolt remote re-pointed to a scratch file:// remote; verify with bd where; compare stats, pre/post export diff, doctor; record tracked-file diffs (hooks, issues.jsonl). (2) Owner pauses ALL bd users: agents local+cloud, git ops (hooks run bd), scheduled jobs, IDE. (3) Old binary, per database: dolt pull, dolt push, second pull shows nothing new; check no dirty ignored tables; baseline stats+doctor; bd export --all; cp -a whole .beads with no bd running. (4) New binary by explicit path, not on PATH: canary on the smallest database, verify vs baseline; then one database at a time, verify each. Do NOT bootstrap worktrees: they share the main clone's database. (5) Push each migrated database only after it verifies. (6) Swap the PATH binary last; upgrade or remove the npm @beads/bd copy; which -a bd shows one version. (7) bd hooks install per project; per-project commits with owner; bd doctor. Rollback before push: restore the .beads copy + old binary. Never force past a gate.
acceptance_criteria: bd version 1.3.0; every clone opens and bd stats matches its pre-upgrade baseline; bd doctor clean or pre-existing only; hooks reinstalled; pre-upgrade JSONL backups kept per clone.
notes:
Owner decisions 2026-09-30: target 1.3.0 (stable, Latest); no other machines or cloud sessions hold clones; skip the no-remote scratch database; dolt push/pull APPROVED.
Rehearsal 2026-09-30 PASSED on copies of all six databases (isolated HOME, file:// remotes): pinned 1.3.0 linux_amd64 checksum OK (bd sha256 fb387d28...); schema 53->66 via smart-gate first-mover path, 1-7s each; stats identical; exports semantically identical (comment and dependency IDs re-keyed); push and second pull OK; hook files unchanged; tracked issues.jsonl rewritten (ID re-key only); 1.1.0 refuses the migrated store (safe failure); rollback by restoring the .beads copy works; 1.3.0 resolves worktrees to the main clone database; pre-migration Dolt status clean everywhere.
Findings: bd doctor is unsupported in embedded mode (drop from acceptance). The migration leaves is_blocked stale on one database (2 rows); bd recompute-blocked (1.3.0) restores baseline stats, so it is a required step.
Harness docs: bd search now includes closed issues by default; one beads skill line says open only (stale, cosmetic).
Next: owner pauses every bd user, then production per database.
Production 2026-09-30: vip-agent canary migrated, verified (stats identical, semantic-diffs=0) and pushed to GitHub Dolt remote via scratchpad/bd-upgrade/upgrade.sh. Side effect: 1.3.0 creates <root>/.beads.gate.lock (permanent flock file; gitignore *.gate.lock*, never delete); vip-agent .gitignore updated, other repos need the same line in their commit. Until the PATH swap, use scratchpad/bd-upgrade/bin/bd in vip-agent (1.1.0 refuses it). Remaining: owner pauses bd users, then preflight/migrate/push for the other five projects; PATH swap; npm copy; per-repo hooks, gitignore and issues.jsonl commits.
2026-09-30 complete except commits: all six databases migrated, verified against baseline, pushed (one included on owner approval). ~/.local/bin/bd is 1.3.0 (sha fb387d28...); 1.1.0 kept at ~/.local/lib/bd/bd-1.1.0; npm @beads/bd removed; which -a bd shows one binary. Every clone and worktree opens and matches its baseline stats. bd hooks install rewrote the tracked .beads/hooks (v1.0.5 -> v1.3.0 marker section) in five repos. Rehearsal missed this because its throwaway repos lacked core.hooksPath. One repo's hooks are in untracked .git/hooks (active before; earlier 'hooks not wired' note was wrong). Pending owner: per-repo commits of hooks, issues.jsonl, interactions.jsonl, and a *.gate.lock* gitignore line. The npm beads-ui package is untested against 1.3.0.
close_reason: Upgrade complete 2026-09-30: all six databases on 1.3.0 (schema v66), verified against baselines, Dolt-pushed; PATH binary 1.3.0, npm copy removed; upgrade-only commits made and pushed in five repos. Held: one repo's push, because a sibling repo in the same workspace already had 14 unpushed commits (owner to decide).

title: Cross-project beads dashboard
description: Local dashboard tracking all beads-backed projects. Page 1: cross-project overview (bd counts open/in_progress/blocked/deferred/closed, active agent work, last ~12 done, needs-you questions/blockers, next pending). Page 2: beads explorer (epic>task>subtask tree, status filters, closed children shown with green check, rollup e.g. open 5/7 beside the stored status, side detail panel per item). Projects registered by folder path in gitignored local config. Beads is sole authority for counts/status; a fixed-format per-task progress file carries narrative + open questions, parsed deterministically (Haiku scraper only as fallback). Read-only over beads. Moved from another project's tracker.
notes:
Open questions: project list; read-only vs answering bd human from UI; '12 lines' meaning (summary length vs recent-task count); live refresh vs on-load. Precondition: bd upgrade (child task). Data-access findings 2026-09-30 (bd 1.3.0, embedded): bd serve and bd sql are unsupported in embedded mode. Reads via bd --readonly --directory : export (all beads, deps, comments; ~0.6-0.9s), --json ready/blocked/human list (~0.3-0.5s); six projects refresh in parallel in ~1s. bd show rewrites .beads/last-touched even under --readonly, so avoid it. human list prints null when empty. 'blocked' has two meanings: stored status=blocked (bd count/list) vs dependency-blocked (bd blocked, status summary). Worktrees share their main clone's DB, so dedupe projects by database. Recommendation drafted in session; see docs/reference/bd-capabilities-1.3.0.md. Hub design (owner 2026-09-30: vip-agent itself is the hub). bd repo was rejected: its repo list is read only from the tracked config.yaml (source-verified); it reads auto-exported JSONL; repo sync pushes via the public Dolt remote. Proposed instead: hub.local/ in vip-agent, gitignored, with its own git repo and no Dolt remote, config seeded before bd init (otherwise init bootstraps from the parent's GitHub remote; verified on a copy). Sync: bd --readonly --directory

export | bd --directory hub.local import -, per project, de-duplicated by database, with paths in a gitignored local file. Import only upserts, so the sync must delete hub beads that vanished at source. Dashboard queries the hub with ordinary bd commands (ready, blocked, human list, count, list, export, graph; show is safe in the hub). Tested on copies: counts and ready match sources; re-import is idempotent; main DB untouched.
